blocks.text: I'll be honest: parking at Bondi on a sunny weekend can test your patience like nothing else. But after years of doing it, I've got a system — where to leave the car for free, when to just pay for the closest station, and the one move that beats the whole lottery. Here it is.

items.label: Free parking
items.value: Residential streets north of Blair St

blocks.title: Read the sign before you walk off
blocks.text: Inspectors patrol Bondi constantly and the fines are steep. Never block a driveway, and always check the sign for time limits and permit zones — a 'permit holders only' block will catch you out even when there's a clear space.

My go-to is the residential streets north of Blair Street, back from the beach. Much of it is free and unrestricted, and it's roughly a 5–7 minute walk down to the sand. On weekdays it's easy until residents get home late afternoon; on weekends it fills through the morning, so get in early. North Bondi is the hardest pocket to crack, but once you're past Blair Street heading away from Campbell Parade, spots open up.

items: Queen Elizabeth Drive car park — the council station directly behind the beach, and by far the largest with around 500 bays. Metered roughly 7am–7pm, seven days; height clearance is about 2.7m, so tall vans and campervans should measure up first. It fills fast on a nice day.
Pacific Bondi car park — beneath the complex opposite the Bondi Pavilion, a two-minute walk to the sand and open long hours daily. Pre-booking online is usually cheaper than the drive-up rate.
Wilson Parking at The Hub (Hall Street) — often overlooked, pricey, but a reliable fallback for an hour or two on a hectic day.
Street meters along Campbell Parade and the shops — handy but the dearest per hour, and time-limited.

blocks.text: If you're down here often, a Waverley Council beach parking permit lets you stay unlimited time in the metered bays on Queen Elizabeth Drive and Park Drive — a genuinely good deal for regulars and worth checking your eligibility for.

blocks.title: What it costs
blocks.text: Beach-adjacent meters are the dearest and get cheaper the further back you go. Council adjusts these rates periodically, so check Waverley Council's current parking fees rather than trusting any fixed figure — including mine.
The move that beats the lottery

On a perfect summer's day, I skip the circling entirely: train to Bondi Junction, then the 333, 380 or 381 bus straight down to Campbell Parade — about a 10–13 minute run. You'll be on the sand while everyone else is still hunting for a bay. If you must drive on a busy day, try the south end around Edward and Francis Streets, or the blocks near the Beach Road Hotel; most people aim for the middle of the beach, so the edges can be surprisingly lucky.

items.q: Is there free parking at Bondi Beach?
items.a: Yes — many residential streets north of Blair Street are free and unrestricted, about a 5–7 minute walk to the beach. Always read the sign, as permit-only blocks are mixed in, and get there early on weekends.

items.q: What's the closest car park to Bondi Beach?
items.a: The Queen Elizabeth Drive car park, the council station right behind the sand with around 500 bays. It's metered roughly 7am–7pm daily and fills quickly, so arrive early.

items.q: Can I get to Bondi without driving?
items.a: Easily. Take the train to Bondi Junction, then the 333, 380 or 381 bus down to Campbell Parade — around 10–13 minutes and no parking stress at all.
